newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's Tarom to stop cooperation with Dac Air.
newsitem.headline: Romania's Tarom to stop cooperation with Dac Air.

text.p: Romania's Tarom SA state airline has ceased cooperation with private airline Dac Air after the latter signed an accord with Hungarian airline Malev, a newspaper reported on Thursday.
But a senior Dac Air executive said the deal it had clinched with Malev posed no threat to the state-run Romanian carrier. He hoped to clarify the matter with Tarom management.

Evenimentul Zilei quoted Tarom general manager Dan Vulcan as saying his airline had stopped all joint projects with Dac Air after it signed an accord to start daily flights with Malev between Budapest and the Romanian cities of Timisoara and Cluj.
Vulcan said Dac Air had signed the Malev deal immediately after agreeing with Tarom on the allocation of external routes.
Tarom officials were unavailable for comment.
"This is a major misunderstanding," Dac Air's vice president Mihai David told Reuters. "It appears that Tarom was not properly informed."
Under the block-space agreement signed with Malev last month, the Hungarian airline will buy a fixed number of seats on each flight operated by Dac Air's Canadian-made DASH-8s.

"This means a guaranteed export of services. What we did was actually identify a niche on the market which was unused by Tarom or other airlines. Nobody is going to be harmed by the deal," David said.
Dac Air, which started international flights last August, is owned by local investor George Paunescu.

Dac Air last year proposed that Tarom, one of its shareholders, take over some domestic and cross-border routes, airport facilities, and booking and ticketing operations under an association agreement.
David said the two airlines had set up a joint group to share out external routes "to avoid financial losses irrespective of whether we are talking about private or state-run airlines."
